clue.text: Critical situation in court — might make light of it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in tennis, the moment when one more point wins the whole contest
second meaning, read literally: the striking tip of a matchstick is what produces a flame

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' sounds like shrugging something off; here it means literally producing light, as the head of a match does when struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The tennis term names the deciding rally, while the literal phrase names the head of a matchstick that ignites.

clue.text: No American prosecutrix, this girl

parts.note: surface reading: a woman who is not a US prosecutor
setter's reading: the girl's name splits as an indefinite article, a male person and the US abbreviation for district attorney, and a prosecutrix is a woman, so she is no such thing

explanation.surface: Someone insists the young woman in question is not an American prosecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the name as A MAN DA: a male district attorney. A prosecutrix, a female prosecutor, is no 'a man DA', which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a common female first name, so it suits a clue asking for some particular girl.

clue.text: Fortresses of the sect laid in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins has been knocked down and lies jumbled, so the letters must be rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious group's strongholds have been reduced to rubble.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortified stronghold commanding a city, so the plural matches fortresses directly.

clue.text: Composer looks alarmed on train trip

parts.note: someone frightened goes white, or pales

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the word before it tumbles out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer travelling by rail looks frightened during the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train trip' reads as a railway journey; 'trip' is really the signal to stumble the letters of train.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestrina was the sixteenth-century Italian master of Renaissance church polyphony.

clue.text: Country has grounds for great annoyance?

parts.note: ire is anger
grounds as in an estate's land

explanation.surface: A nation is said to have good reason to be very irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds for' reads as 'reasons for'; it is land followed by ire, read as grounds placed after the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is an island nation west of Great Britain, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: A number of sportsmen behead the old engine-driver

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the top, which in a word means its first letter goes

parts.note: old locomotives were driven by steam power

explanation.surface: A group of athletes is told to decapitate a veteran train driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine-driver' suggests a person at the controls; here it is the force that drove old engines.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a side of players, a group of sportsmen competing together.

clue.text: Disciplinarian mounts number one vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: one number among many
the Roman numeral
a tram is a street vehicle on rails

explanation.surface: A strict figure climbs aboard the leading vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules, named after a stern seventeenth-century French drillmaster.

clue.text: Tempt into wrong-doing involving salary date

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the letters that follow are tangled together

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is lured into crime by something to do with payday.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is an idiom for guiding them off the right path into sin or error.

clue.text: Property in Maryland, for instance ?

wordplay.note: Maryland is an eastern US state: E for east, then the word for what it is

explanation.surface: Someone is describing a piece of real estate in Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Maryland' looks like a location; Maryland is really an example of an East-coast state.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land owned by one person, so it is property in the legal sense.

clue.text: It's a bell that could be used in prison

indicators.note: the letters could be put to another use, rearranged to make a new word

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A bell might serve some purpose inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state jail, stormed in 1789 at the start of the Revolution.

clue.text: Deplored one being late ?

definitions.note: an adjective describing such a person, not a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: as in the phrase 'the late ...', said of someone dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like unpunctual, but it means dead, as in 'the late Mr Smith'; the stock phrase 'late lamented' supplies the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to mourn or bewail, and a lamented person is a dead one who is mourned.

clue.text: -Purpose or advantage of rice beer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in 'for the ... of', meaning for the benefit or purpose of
second meaning: the Japanese drink brewed from fermented rice

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is the point of a Japanese drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for someone's sake means for their benefit or end, and the homograph is the Japanese fermented rice drink.

clue.text: They may carry dishes for perhaps eleven empty poets

parts.note: eleven players make a cricket or football side
a bard is a poet; the empty ones have nothing inside them
empty means holding nothing, and nothing is the round figure nought

explanation.surface: Pieces of furniture, or waiters, might serve dishes to a team of hungry versifiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' supplies O, nothing, which goes inside the poets. Eleven is the number in a cricket or football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a dining-room cabinet with a flat top on which serving plates are set.

clue.text: Agents collected about 5 kinds of fruit

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round the other
things collected are gathered up in a heap, so the letters are scooped together and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 5 down is a country whose poetic name is this

explanation.surface: Secret agents gathered round five varieties of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a number of fruits; it points to the answer to 5 down, and Erin is the poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerines are small sweet citrus oranges with loose peel, so they are sorts of fruit.

clue.text: Letters written with a list for renewal of necessary things

parts.note: two letters written out as words: ess for S and en for N

indicators.note: something renewed is made over afresh, so the letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone renewing a shopping list writes out the things they cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters written' means letters spelt out as words, ESS and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentials are the indispensable items one cannot manage without, so they are needed things.

clue.text: Like measures needed to get right wine in Washington district ?

indicators.note: one part sits inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: Washington DC, the District of Columbia
R is the abbreviation for right
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Extreme steps may be required to obtain the correct wine in the US capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic is the stock word for severe action, as in the phrase 'drastic measures', so it describes the kind needed.

clue.text: He represents posterity's cause

parts.note: surface reading: an advocate or lawyer arguing on behalf of future generations
setter's reading: cause means origin, and a forebear is the source from whom all descendants come

explanation.surface: A campaigner speaks up for the interests of future generations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' reads as a campaign being championed; it means the origin from which later generations spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather is literally the origin of his descendants, so he is the reason later generations exist.

clue.text: David's church 18

parts.note: surface reading: some church belonging to a man called David
setter's reading: 18 down's answer is the words of an opera, and King David's psalms are the words sung in church

explanation.surface: A reference to a particular church called David's, with a cross-reference attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 down's answer is LIBRETTO, the text of a sung work. Tradition credits King David with the Psalms, so the book of them is his church libretto.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a volume of the Psalms, traditionally attributed to King David, arranged for singing at services.

clue.text: Book for entertainment?

parts.note: surface reading: a novel read for fun, or reserving seats at a show
setter's reading: the book of an opera or musical is its written text

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like reserve tickets or a novel; in theatre the book is the script of a musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, known in the theatre as its book.

clue.text: Composer writes up short script and foreign articles

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript
French and Latin for and
the two English indefinite articles, an and a

explanation.surface: A composer pens an abbreviated text and some pieces from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the nineteenth-century Czech composer of Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Game player ? Nonsense !

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
gammon is old slang for humbug or rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a games player's claims.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammon in this sense is British slang for nonsense, besides being a cut of ham.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Inter-town in Greater Manchester

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to place a body in a grave
second meaning: a mill town north of Manchester in north-west England

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'Inter-town' look like a word for travel between towns; 'Inter' is the verb meaning to place in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a corpse is to put it in the ground, and the same word names a Lancashire mill town.

clue.text: Surviving trace of 100-litre mixture

indicators.note: a mixture stirs its ingredients together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some residue remains from a hundred litres of a blend.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is a remnant left over from an earlier time, such as a species or landform that has survived.

clue.text: Old French paper money gains on exchange, in a way
Fine steed to carry one home !

indicators.note: the phrase before is said to carry something within it, inside its letters

parts.note: letters inside the phrase, across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: A splendid horse bears its rider back to the stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its dwelling, and figuratively any snug place of residence.

clue.text: A swan-song for him ?

parts.note: surface reading: a farewell performance for some man
setter's reading: a swan-song is a last appearance before death, and for a beast taken to slaughter that last appearance happens in one particular building

explanation.surface: Someone is giving a final farewell performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A swan-song is a final act before dying, after the legend that swans sing only just before death; 'him' is the animal sent to be killed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where livestock are killed, so it is the scene of an animal's final moments.

clue.text: Bertie Wooster's friends — the medical sort ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: members of the idle young men's club in P. G. Wodehouse's stories
second meaning, split in two: DR, the doctor's title, plus ONES, as in 'the doctor ones'

explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, P. G. Wodehouse's comic hero, belongs to a London gentlemen's club of idlers; read whimsically, the answer is also DR ONES, doctor types.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wodehouse club members are idle loafers named after male bees, and the split form means the doctoring kind.

clue.text: People are sent in them, in both senses

definitions.text: People are sent in them, in both senses

parts.words: People are sent in them, in both senses
parts.note: surface reading: vehicles or ships that people are dispatched in

parts.words: People are sent in them, in both senses
parts.note: setter's reading: to be sent is also slang for being thrilled, so the word also means states of rapture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' means both dispatched and, in old slang, carried away with delight; the plural noun covers both conveyances and ecstasies.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ships carrying troops or convicts and fits of overwhelming joy or emotion.
